title: a capability read written directly at module top level, outside every provide scope, is an unsatisfied requirement charged to the module
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction': 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' Module top level is exactly where the compiler knows the complete closure — there is no caller left to propagate to — and `unsatisfied-top-level-requirement` has pinned that since the area was written. It pins it for an INDIRECT read: a top-level call to a function whose inferred row names the capability. This case is the direct spelling of the identical program, and it was escapable by inlining the read until 2026-08-26: `checkLayerSatisfaction`'s top-level visit charged a resolved top-level CALLEE and never consulted the read itself, because the machinery that recognizes `Capability.context()` runs per function body and module top level is not a function body. Both backends measured `ok: true` with zero diagnostics on this file, and the reference lane ran it: `Panic: capability 'Directory' was not provided`. A one-line program shape the corpus already pinned was open in its one-line form. That is the whole content of the case, and it is why it belongs beside `unsatisfied-top-level-requirement` rather than instead of it: the pair is the evidence that the rule reads the requirement and not the call graph. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: `messageContains`. `an-unsatisfied-top-level-requirement-names-exactly-the-capability` declares one, and it is right to, because that case exists to catch a refusal naming the WRONG requirement — its program has a capability that could be named wrongly. This program declares exactly one capability, so there is no wrong-but-plausible name a refusal could carry, and the two backends render a row set differently anyway (`Directory` on the reference, `{Directory}` on the fork), so a fragment here would pin nothing this case is about. The failure mode this case has to exclude is an EMPTY row, and an empty row produces no SMITHERS2102 at all — the code and position carry that by themselves. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column from 22 to 21 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 8d13a2722a7ad2993fababe6c0500991097bd1a6825c13011709ec3a7db96c2b before and after). The paired positive control is `a-capability-read-inside-a-callback-charges-the-caller`, whose read is reached from a top-level `Layer.provide` computation and must keep compiling and RUNNING, so a rule that charges every top-level-reachable read turns that case red instead of passing quietly.
